project.name: WORTH Store Roadmap 2 S.6 Hardware-Aware I/O, QoS, And Background Work Pacing

phases.title: Backend And Media Capability Admission
acceptance: Backend and media capability admission produces sealed witnesses with evidence class, rebind triggers, support posture, and confidence limits.
Raw backend labels, config strings, OS names, probes, environment variables, terminal projections, and copied rows cannot mint stronger capability.
Unsupported, unavailable, unknown, stale, and rebind-required posture deny typed before direct I/O, mmap, async, fsync, directory-sync, durable rename, or secure-frame claims are consumed.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 1 from the spec. Freeze backend/media capability vocabulary and authority before any scheduler path can claim hardware-aware behavior. Preserve evidence-class strength and keep certification as executed-law proof, not runtime authority.
phases.qa_focus: Look for raw capability labels, confidence laundering, backend-selected durability semantics, missing rebind triggers, support posture collapse, and Foundational/Proof evidence replacing Store witnesses.

phases.title: Foreground Lane Contracts And Reservation Admission
acceptance: Foreground physical lanes, resource units, latency envelope kinds, and reservation states are Store-owned contracts, not best-effort labels.
Reservation admission consumes backend/media capability, S.5 stable-read readiness, S.5.1 security readiness, and lane envelope evidence.
Foreground fairness covers point reads, range reads, commit-critical WAL writes, ordinary page writes, interactive reads, and internal foreground reads without priority laundering.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 2. Make reservation admission explicit, typed, and denied before physical I/O when required capacity, capability, or security/stability evidence is missing.
phases.qa_focus: Look for priority flags, semantic labels driving physical priority, missing resource units, undeclared foreground-vs-foreground arbitration, and successful reservations that should be violated or denied.

phases.title: Background Work Classes And Pacing Policy
acceptance: Background classes are I/O pressure shapes with distinct pacing outcomes for yield, defer, deny, throttle, admit-with-debt, and violation.
Idle-capacity borrowing uses revocable leases tied to foreground reservations and backend/media capability.
Background debt remains visible through typed counters and cannot hide in logs, elapsed time, or worker-local state.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 3. Model compaction, checkpoint, scrub, replication prep, blob pressure, backup prep, and repair pressure by physical I/O pressure shape only, without importing later semantic lifecycle work.
phases.qa_focus: Look for generic background labels, unrevoked idle borrowing, hidden debt, worker-local queues bypassing foreground counters, and background work silently becoming foreground.

phases.title: Queue Admission, Grouping, And Backpressure Execution
acceptance: Admitted queue work lowers to execution plans that preserve lane class, reservation, security scope, durability posture, and grouping basis.
Execution may adapt mechanically within admitted policy but may not reclassify work, strengthen claims, hide debt, or alter durability/security meaning.
Grouping, read-ahead, write-back, and backpressure outcomes are typed and replay-visible.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 4. Build queue admission and execution lowering that makes positive grouping bases and backpressure causes explicit.
phases.qa_focus: Look for queue-internal authority, grouping by absence of known danger, untyped backpressure, starvation through grouping, and execution-time policy mutation.

phases.title: Flush, Sync, Rename, And Durability Ordering
acceptance: Durability ordering has backend-neutral states for flush, fdatasync/fsync, directory sync, rename, checkpoint, WAL, and manifest publication.
Unknown, unsupported, stale, or externally-guaranteed durability posture remains visible and cannot satisfy stronger certified APIs.
Crash/recovery tests prove ordering decisions without relying on backend-specific accidental behavior.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 5. Admit durability semantics before execution and keep durable rename/directory sync/flush ordering exact across backend profiles.
phases.qa_focus: Look for backend-chosen semantics, fsync/fdatasync collapse, missing directory sync, durable rename optimism, and crash tests that only prove the host machine.

phases.title: Page-Cache, Mmap, And Direct-I/O Access Policy
acceptance: Buffered, mmap, direct-I/O, and mixed-mode access have admitted coherence, alignment, fault, and security posture.
Unsupported or unknown access-mode posture denies typed before execution.
Mmap faults, page-cache visibility, direct-I/O alignment, and mixed-mode invalidation are observable through Store outcomes and counters.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 6. Keep access mode policy physical and explicit; do not let an execution path discover coherence semantics after it has already touched bytes.
phases.qa_focus: Look for implicit OS page-cache trust, direct-I/O alignment guesses, mixed-mode incoherence, mmap fault swallowing, and security scope stripped during access-mode transitions.

phases.title: Trim, Punch-Hole, And Cold-Tier I/O Posture
acceptance: Trim, punch-hole, sparse, and cold-tier postures distinguish physical zeros, logical holes, unavailable bytes, and non-observable reclaimed storage.
S.5 protected reachability and S.5.1 security scope survive space reclamation and cold-tier policy.
S.6 exposes non-claim handoffs only; it does not implement S.7 placement or S.10 compaction semantics.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 7. Define cold and reclaimed storage I/O posture without turning it into compaction or tier-placement authority.
phases.qa_focus: Look for hole/zero collapse, protected-byte loss, cold-tier claims masquerading as placement readiness, and reclaim operations bypassing security/read stability.

phases.title: Security-Scope And Secure-I/O Preservation
acceptance: S.5.1 security scope is preserved through reservation, grouping, batching, read-ahead, write-back, background leases, repair scans, and verification pressure.
Secure-I/O unsupported posture denies typed rather than degrading to ordinary platform I/O.
Identity-provider claims, key ids, IAM roles, operator identities, and terminal projections cannot become S.6 secure-I/O authority.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 8. Bind secure-I/O preservation to the real scheduler and backend paths, not only to certification rows.
phases.qa_focus: Look for scope laundering through batching, repair/backup scans reading too broadly, secure posture downgrade, raw identity leakage, and certification-owned security authority.

phases.title: Latency Envelope And Interference Counter Model
acceptance: Latency envelope and interference counters declare strength as exact, bounded, sampled, derived, certification-only, or unavailable.
Replay is deterministic for policy decisions, counter topology, and proof progression, not OS wall-clock timing.
Post-admission violations are typed outcomes with causal attribution.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 9. Make latency and interference evidence precise enough to support adversarial harnesses without pretending every timing measurement is exact.
phases.qa_focus: Look for wall-clock determinism claims, sampled counters treated as exact, violation logs instead of outcomes, missing causal attribution, and counter topology hidden from replay.

phases.title: S.4.5 I/O Pressure Harness Extension
acceptance: The S.4.5 harness gains backend, actor, driver, fault, pressure, and oracle support for S.6 I/O pressure simulations.
Fault evidence classes distinguish simulated, injected, observed-host, certified-backend, and externally-guaranteed behavior.
Simulated backend success cannot certify real backend safety without explicit qualification.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 10. Extend the existing harness rather than creating a separate test island, and keep evidence strength honest.
phases.qa_focus: Look for synthetic-only tests pretending to be real, missing oracle state, simulated-to-certified laundering, harness APIs that are harder than production APIs, and non-replayable pressure cases.

phases.title: Cross-Backend Qualification Matrix
acceptance: Qualification matrix rows bind backend profile, media assumptions, evidence class, capability support, rebind triggers, and test/harness proof.
Stale, unverifiable, config-only, probe-only, and externally-guaranteed rows cannot satisfy stronger certified-backend APIs.
Cross-backend parity tests cover equivalent policy results without erasing backend-specific denial causes.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 11. Make the matrix a qualification/evidence publication surface, not a runtime authority source.
phases.qa_focus: Look for stale matrix rows used as current authority, evidence strength collapse, backend-specific cause loss, and row ids replacing Store witnesses.

phases.title: S.7/S.10/S.11 Readiness And Non-Claim Handoffs
acceptance: S.6 produces distinct non-claim handoffs for S.7 placement, S.10 compaction, and S.11 operator readiness.
Handoffs expose only I/O posture, limits, counters, and non-claim markers; they do not authorize later semantics.
Cross-substitution between placement, compaction, and operator-readiness handoffs is compile-fail or typed denial.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 12. Give later milestones enough physical I/O evidence to consume while making impossible phases impossible.
phases.qa_focus: Look for S.7/S.10/S.11 authority smuggled into S.6, one generic future-readiness blob, missing non-claim markers, and handoff substitution.

phases.title: Certification Evidence Materialization And API Adoption Proof
acceptance: Certification materializes executed S.6 evidence from Store-owned witnesses, receipts, counters, and proof progression.
Public adoption tests prove real APIs consume the new S.6 authority surfaces rather than parallel certification-only contracts.
Foundational and Proof evidence is named and bounded where used, without becoming runtime authority.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 13. Prove the APIs are actually adopted in production crates and that certification remains courtroom evidence over executed Store law.
phases.qa_focus: Look for certification-only implementation, test-only authority paths, unused production constructors, proof rows replacing Store witnesses, and missing public adoption examples.

phases.title: Production Readiness Closure And Later-Milestone Admission
acceptance: S.6 closeout consumes Phase 13 materialized evidence and publishes sealed readiness for hardware-aware I/O, QoS, and background pacing.
Residual non-claims and later-milestone debts are explicit, typed, and not accidentally satisfied by S.6.
Focused verification, line-cap checks, compile-fail coverage, integration tests, and closeout evidence are complete for the milestone.
phases.instructions: Implement S.6 Phase 14. Close the milestone without expanding it into S.7, S.10, S.11, or real-world backend certification beyond the spec's admitted evidence classes.
phases.qa_focus: Look for premature readiness, hidden residual debt, overclaiming later milestones, broad green tests masking missing compile-fail coverage, and certification proof without production adoption.
